title: Brookfield takes 99-year lease on Kushner family's 666 Fifth Avenue office property
description_short: Brookfield takes 99-year lease on Kushner family's 666 Fifth Avenue office property
description_medium: Reuters reported that Brookfield acquired a 99-year lease on the office portion of 666 Fifth Avenue in August 2018. A separate Reuters report said Qatar Investment Authority was not involved in that lease transaction. These reports do not establish a June 2017 Qatari bailout, a $1.8 billion payment, or an exchange of investment for favorable treatment.
description_long:
Brookfield acquired a 99-year lease on the office portion of 666 Fifth Avenue, the Kushner family's heavily indebted Manhattan property, in August 2018, Reuters reported. A separate Reuters report on Qatar's investment strategy said the Qatar Investment Authority was not involved in the Brookfield lease transaction. This later lease is a discrete, documented development concerning the property.

The sources reviewed do not substantiate the frozen claim that Qatar bailed out the building in June 2017 or that a $1.8 billion Qatari payment rescued it. They also do not establish a quid pro quo between an investment and government treatment. The narrower corrected claim is limited to Brookfield's 99-year lease and the reported absence of QIA involvement in that deal; it should not be presented as evidence of a Qatar bailout. Reuters described a lease restructuring of the property, not a purchase of it by Qatar.

The event should be described as contributions to the inaugural committee and, if included, the executive's attributed statement about dinner access. The frozen reference to an inaugural ball and any implied exchange for policy are not supported by the sources reviewed. The distinction matters because committee fundraising and dinner access are separate reported facts.

title: Trump announces proposed 30% tariffs on EU and Mexico, with an August 1 start date
description_short: Trump announces proposed 30% tariffs on EU and Mexico, with an August 1 start date
description_medium: On July 12, 2025, President Trump announced proposed 30% tariffs on imports from the European Union and Mexico, with an August 1 start date stated in letters to the trading partners. Reuters reported the announcement. The report establishes a tariff threat and proposed schedule, not that the tariffs ultimately took effect on that date.
description_long:
President Donald Trump announced on July 12, 2025, that the United States would impose 30% tariffs on imports from the European Union and Mexico. Letters sent to the trading partners stated an August 1 start date, Reuters reported. The event was an announcement of proposed tariffs and a negotiating deadline, rather than evidence that the tariffs had already been collected.

The frozen record's July 28 date does not match the reported announcement date. The source supports describing the 30% rate and proposed August 1 start date, but the outcome should not imply implementation without a separate source documenting the tariffs' later status. This corrected claim is limited to Trump's July 12 announcement and the date proposed in the letters. The announcement is the sourced event; later implementation should be checked independently. It also does not document subsequent negotiations, modifications, or collections under the announced tariff schedule; those would be separate developments with their own evidence.

title: House Oversight Democrats report $7.8 million in foreign-government payments to Trump properties
description_short: House Oversight Democrats report $7.8 million in foreign-government payments to Trump properties
description_medium: A House Oversight Democrats report said at least 20 foreign governments paid $7.8 million to four Trump properties during Donald Trump's presidency. The finding is attributed to the committee minority's report. It does not establish that the payments began on inauguration day or that a court found an Emoluments Clause violation.
description_long:
House Oversight Democrats reported that at least 20 foreign governments paid a total of $7.8 million to four Trump properties during Donald Trump's presidency. The committee release describes payments to businesses associated with the president while he held office and presents them as relevant to Emoluments Clause concerns.

The source is a report released by the Democratic minority on the House Oversight Committee, so the finding should be attributed to that report. It is not a judicial ruling. The evidence reviewed does not establish that foreign governments began booking a Trump hotel on inauguration day, and the report itself does not prove a court found a constitutional violation. The narrower claim records the reported total, number of governments and properties, and time period while preserving attribution. The cited release links to the report and states the committee's reported findings. These distinctions preserve the limits of the committee's reported evidence.

That the report itself proves an Emoluments Clause violation or a judicial finding of one.
